evals.prompt:
Review this Tailwind v4 markup:
Report
. The project IntelliSense diagnostic recommends print:flex. A status badge currently builds bg-${color}-600 for red or green. Show corrected class usage without adding dependencies. The editor/LSP is unavailable in this session; explain what you can verify. Also explain whether you would introduce v4-only syntax if this were an existing v3 project.
evals.expected_output: Canonical print utility, complete status class literals, and honest version-aware verification.
expectations: Uses print:flex for the supplied diagnostic.
Selects complete bg-red-600 and bg-green-600 literals instead of interpolating class fragments.
Does not suppress or disable suggestCanonicalClasses.
Discloses unavailable diagnostic verification and does not equate a build with zero warnings.
Preserves v3 compatibility without an unsolicited upgrade.

evals.prompt:
A plain CSS project already uses BEM. Correct this markup and describe matching selector changes:

Pack

. Preserve the DOM structure and existing styling approach. No Tailwind migration.
evals.expected_output: Flat BEM element names and a modifier alongside its base class.
expectations: Retains product-card--featured and adds the product-card base class.
Replaces product-card__header__title with product-card__title in markup and selector guidance.
Preserves DOM structure and BEM styling without adding Tailwind.
Avoids deep descendant selectors.

evals.prompt: Show stylesheet names, class names, and module mapping access for two independent components, without writing a full framework component. A new ProfileCard uses CSS Modules and no BEM convention. An existing ProductCard module intentionally uses product-card and product-card__title; keep BEM there. Both need an active state. Explain how you would scope a third-party .vendor-label override inside ProfileCard, reuse shared tokens, preserve focus, and respect reduced motion if adding animation.
evals.expected_output: Colocated modules with simple local names for ProfileCard and optional preserved BEM for ProductCard.
expectations: Uses colocated *.module.css files and simple camelCase local names for ProfileCard.
Preserves optional BEM for ProductCard with bracket access for hyphenated module keys.
Combines base and active/modifier classes.
Limits the global vendor override beneath a local wrapper.
Reuses tokens and preserves visible focus and reduced-motion behavior.
Does not impose BEM on ProfileCard or migrate either component to Tailwind.

evals.prompt: Create the color-token structure for a new Tailwind v4 theme with primary, secondary and tertiary roles. Use an existing neutral palette plus a new ocean color family. Show the complete ocean scale and all background, border and text aliases, then style a card and an amber warning badge. Raw color values must stay in palette definitions. Include equivalent plain CSS consumption and explain v3 compatibility. Do not build an app.
evals.expected_output: An eleven-stop named palette, nine semantic aliases, correct CSS/Tailwind token consumption, and no literal component colors.
expectations: Defines ocean-50, ocean-100 through ocean-900 in steps of 100, and ocean-950 centrally.
Uses primary/secondary/tertiary for backgrounds, stroke-prefixed tokens for borders, and foreground-prefixed tokens for text.
Semantic aliases reference palette tokens; component declarations do not contain raw hex, RGB, HSL, or OKLCH colors.
Uses bg-primary, border-stroke-primary and text-foreground-primary rather than confusing SVG stroke utilities with borders.
Uses a named amber palette token for the out-of-role badge color.
Uses version-appropriate theme registration, keeping v4 directives out of v3 configuration.
Distinguishes illustrative palette values from verified contrast.

evals.prompt: A vendor button rule overrides our color. Both stylesheets use normal declarations in the same author layer: vendor has .vendor-panel .button { color: var(--foreground-secondary); }, and our earlier .button rule uses var(--foreground-primary). Fix the scoped override without changing vendor markup or adding important. Explain what changes if the immutable vendor declaration is already important, and whether moving a class to the end of the HTML class attribute helps.
evals.expected_output: A scoped selector with suitable specificity and stylesheet order, token colors, and an accurately bounded last-resort exception.
expectations: Uses a scoped selector of sufficient specificity with appropriate source order for the normal-declaration conflict.
Retains token-based text colors.
Does not use important for the solvable normal-declaration conflict.
Explains that HTML class order does not determine cascade priority.
Does not claim increased normal specificity beats an important declaration.
Allows only a narrowly scoped, explained important exception after checking supported customization and cascade options for the immutable important case.
